prompt: Why does `keyscan.py` print each value masked?

choices.text: Masked values are shorter and fit the table
choices.why: Width is not the reason.

choices.text: It would put the secret in the build log
choices.why: Right: the build log is read by more people than the code.

choices.text: The mask makes the key stop working
choices.why: Masking the printout changes nothing about the key.

choices.text: A masked value is what the allow list matches
choices.why: The allow list matches the fingerprint.

prompt: Without the allow list, how many findings does `keyscan.py` report in the repository?
`app/payments.py` and `prompts/support.txt` share the fingerprint `9f8dfa2fe8d2`. What does that say?

choices.text: Both files were written on the same day
choices.why: A fingerprint says nothing about dates.

choices.text: The two files are copies of each other
choices.why: One is Python and one is a prompt; only the key is shared.

choices.text: The same key is written in two places
choices.why: Right: removing it from one file and not the other fixes nothing.

choices.text: Two different keys collided in the hash
choices.why: Twelve hex digits make a collision between two values very unlikely.

prompt: Why does an allow-list line name a fingerprint and not only the file?
hint: What if a real key is pasted into the same document?

choices.text: A real key pasted in that file still fails
choices.why: Right: the exception covers one value, not the whole file.

choices.text: Fingerprints are shorter to type than paths
choices.why: The line carries both anyway.

choices.text: The scanner cannot read file names
choices.why: It prints them in every line.

choices.text: Documentation files are never scanned
choices.why: `docs/storage.md` was scanned and reported.

prompt: What does a line of the allow list carry? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: the file
choices.why: Yes: the path the finding is in.

choices.text: the fingerprint of the value
choices.why: Yes: one exact value.

choices.text: the reason it is accepted
choices.why: Yes: an exception is a written decision.

choices.text: the key itself
choices.why: The allow list would then be one more place the key is written.

choices.text: the date the key expires
choices.why: `keyscan.py` has no dates; `keys.py` does.

prompt: Where does the lesson put the payments key?

choices.text: In the system prompt, with a sentence asking for secrecy
choices.why: A sentence is a request; the key can still reach a reply.

choices.text: In a comment beside the code that calls the API
choices.why: A comment is still in the repository.

choices.text: In the `.env` file committed with the code
choices.why: That is one of the findings.

choices.text: With the refund tool, read from a secret store
choices.why: Right: the model proposes the call and never sees the key.

prompt: Why is a key in the system prompt worse than the same key only in the code?

choices.text: Prompts are stored in plain text and code is not
choices.why: Both are plain text; the difference is where they travel.

choices.text: It reaches replies and every prompt log
choices.why: Right: the call log, the provider's logs and any debug trace.

choices.text: The provider bills extra tokens for keys
choices.why: Cost is not the risk.

choices.text: A model cannot call an API without seeing its key
choices.why: A tool calls the API; the model only proposes.

prompt: Match each finding to where the lesson says its credential belongs.
hint: One place on the right is none of them.

pairs.right: a secret store, read at start-up
with the tool, never in the prompt

right_distractors: an encrypted comment in the code

prompt: A key was pushed to a public repository yesterday, and the line was deleted today. What does the lesson say is still needed?

choices.text: Rotate it: a new key deployed, the old one revoked
choices.why: Right: the history and every clone still hold the old one.

choices.text: Nothing, because the current version is clean
choices.why: The key is in the history and in every clone.

choices.text: A sentence in the README asking people not to use it
choices.why: That asks; it does not revoke.

choices.text: Add its fingerprint to the allow list
choices.why: That hides a real key from the scanner.

prompt: Deleting the line is not the fix for a key that reached a repository; the fix is to ___ it.
hint: Issue a new one, revoke the old one.

prompt: How many of the four keys break at least one rule?
Only `issue_refund` uses the payments key. Why does its scope still fail?
hint: What could a leaked copy do?

choices.text: Payout keys cost more to issue
choices.why: Cost is not the argument.

choices.text: Refund keys must also be able to read
choices.why: The refund tool needs only refund.

choices.text: A leak could also send payouts, for nothing gained
choices.why: Right: least privilege, applied to credentials.

choices.text: The scope list is longer than the limit allows
choices.why: There is no limit on length; the rule compares with what is needed.

prompt: How many days had passed since the payments key was rotated, on 9 October?
An incident asks: this key leaked, what can somebody do with it, and what breaks if we revoke it? Which two fields of the inventory answer?

choices.text: `kept_in` and `rotated`
choices.why: Those say where it lives and how old it is.

choices.text: `name` and `max_age_days`
choices.why: Neither says what the key opens.

choices.text: `needs` and `rotated`
choices.why: `needs` belongs to components, not keys.

choices.text: `scope` and `used_by`
choices.why: Right: what it may do, and who stops working.

prompt: A new tool, `send_invoice`, will use the `orders-db` key and needs only `read`. After adding it to `used_by` and `needs`, does `orders-db` still break SCOPE?

choices.text: No, because two components now share it
choices.why: Sharing does not make write needed.

choices.text: Yes, since nobody needs `write`
choices.why: Right: the rule compares the scope with the union of what users need.

choices.text: No, because adding a user rotates the key
choices.why: Nothing rotates a key except somebody rotating it.

choices.text: Yes, because a key may serve only one tool
choices.why: Sharing is allowed; unused permission is not.

prompt: Put the steps of rotating a key in order.
items: Deploy it to every component that uses the key
Check that they work with the new key

prompt: Which rules does `keys.py` check? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: KEPT, where the key lives
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: SCOPE, what it may do beyond what is needed
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: AGE, the days since rotation
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: the length of the key
choices.why: The inventory never holds the key itself.

choices.text: who created the key
choices.why: The inventory does not record it.

prompt: `log-store` works perfectly and breaks only AGE. Why does the lesson still care?

choices.text: A key never rotated is one nobody knows how to rotate
choices.why: Right: the day it leaks is a bad day to learn how.

choices.text: Old keys get slower over time
choices.why: A key does not slow down.

choices.text: The provider deletes keys after 90 days
choices.why: Ninety days is Tarefa's own policy.

choices.text: Logs written with an old key are unreadable
choices.why: Rotation does not change data already written.
